claim: Curated 'normal events' in CARE (wind) and PreDist (district heating) are quieter than ordinary normal operation of the same assets (alarm rate 16% vs 37% on random eligible 7-day windows; rate ratio 0.30-0.61 over 4 detectors), so balanced benchmarks are optimistic through negative-sample selection in addition to the 50/50 base rate.
notes: opened=true means abstract or full text retrieved in this session (OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index, arXiv HTML, MDPI PDF, Zenodo package). Semantic Scholar not used. No paper found that compares curated vs random normal windows for any energy benchmark. Discrepancy to fix in manuscript: CARE paper states 51 normal datasets; Zenodo v6 (used by us and later papers) has 50.

papers.title: CARE to Compare: A Real-World Benchmark Dataset for Early Fault Detection in Wind Turbine Data
papers.what_it_shows: Full text read. Sec 3.1.3: 'The normal labels have been determined by a combination of feedback of the wind farm operators, manual inspection of the data, and expert knowledge.' Requirement 4: dataset must be balanced. Paper reports 44 anomaly / 51 normal datasets (Zenodo v6 used by later papers: 45/50). Accuracy on normal events counts only normal-status points. Discussion/limitations address only label uncertainty of anomaly starts; no statement that normal events are easier or unrepresentative of routine operation; no comparison with random normal windows.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Confirms the mechanism exists (normal events hand-selected by operator feedback + manual inspection + expert knowledge) but does not acknowledge or measure the resulting optimism.

papers.title: Enabling predictive maintenance in district heating substations: A labelled dataset and fault detection evaluation framework based on service data (PreDist)
papers.what_it_shows: Full text read. 'We also provide a set of pre-defined normal events. For these intervals, well-performing fault detection algorithms should not raise false alarms ... The normal events are selected across all seasons, primarily for substations in the reports list and several additional substations without faults. These intervals are free from maintenance tasks and faults.' 65 normal events (30 M1 / 35 M2). Limitation 2 ('Normal-event definition and unlabelled faults'): 'Normal events could be refined to better represent all stable operating regimes across seasons and control modes. An option would be to generate these automatically ... and evaluate the models' ability to recognise normal behaviour on randomly selected events', noting unlabelled faults may require visual inspection. Separately states reliability is overestimated because the evaluation set is balanced.
papers.overlap_with_claim: CLOSEST PRIOR WORK. The authors themselves flag that pre-defined normal events may not represent all operating regimes and propose random normal events as future work, but do not run that comparison, do not quantify a false-alarm gap, and do not state the direction (easier negatives -> optimism). Our result empirically executes and quantifies their suggested check. Must be cited and credited explicitly.

papers.title: Problems of Spectrum and Bias in Evaluating the Efficacy of Diagnostic Tests (Ransohoff & Feinstein)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: unless an appropriately broad spectrum is chosen for diseased and nondiseased patients, the test may receive falsely high 'rule-in' and 'rule-out' performance.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Established analogue: a too-narrow (too healthy) nondiseased spectrum inflates specificity. Our curated normal events = narrow nondiseased spectrum.

papers.title: Empirical Evidence of Design-Related Bias in Studies of Diagnostic Tests (Lijmer et al.)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: 218 evaluations; studies using a diseased population and a separate control group overestimated diagnostic performance vs clinical-population studies (RDOR 3.0, 95% CI 2.0-4.5).
papers.overlap_with_claim: Quantified medical analogue of 'curated controls' (diagnostic case-control design). Our benchmark = case-control design with selected controls.

papers.title: Evidence of bias and variation in diagnostic accuracy studies (Rutjes et al.)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: 31 meta-analyses/487 studies; highest accuracy estimates in studies with severe cases and healthy controls (RDOR 4.9, 95% CI 0.6-37.3); nonconsecutive inclusion RDOR 1.5.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Directly the 'healthy controls too healthy' analogue; note wide CI. (Task brief said Rutjes 2005; the peer-reviewed article found is CMAJ 2006.)

papers.title: Sources of Variation and Bias in Studies of Diagnostic Accuracy: A Systematic Review (Whiting et al.)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: best-documented effects include disease prevalence and severity, partial verification bias, etc.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Background on spectrum/selection effects.

papers.title: QUADAS-2: A Revised Tool for the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (Whiting et al.)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: 4 domains incl. 'patient selection' assessed for risk of bias and applicability.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Its patient-selection domain (case-control design / inappropriate exclusions signalling questions, known from the tool; only abstract read now) is the checklist item our finding maps to.

papers.title: Spectrum Bias or Spectrum Effect? Subgroup Variation in Diagnostic Test Evaluation (Mulherin & Miller)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: proposes 'spectrum effect'; performance varies across subgroups; study samples must represent the relevant population.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Terminology choice: our curated-vs-random gap is a spectrum effect on the negative class.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of the MoCA ... Avoiding spectrum bias caused by healthy controls
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: specificity 73% with healthy controls vs 37% with referred non-impaired comparisons, same test and cutoff.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Closest design analogue in medicine: same test/threshold, specificity on curated healthy controls vs realistic negatives. Structurally identical to our 16% vs 37% alarm-rate comparison.

papers.title: Impact of spectrum bias on deep learning-based stroke MRI analysis
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: excluding diagnostically uncertain cases led to a four-fold increase in diagnostic odds ratio of a DL tool.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Spectrum bias applied to ML evaluation (medical imaging); not energy, not time series.

papers.title: Choosing negative examples for the prediction of protein-protein interactions (Ben-Hur & Noble)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: the common way of choosing negatives yields high-quality non-interacting sets but 'can lead to biased estimates of prediction accuracy, because the constraints placed on the distribution of the negative examples makes the task easier'.
papers.overlap_with_claim: ML analogue of exactly our mechanism (constrained/curated negatives make the task easier -> optimistic accuracy). Different domain (bioinformatics, not time-series/energy).

papers.title: Revisiting the negative example sampling problem for predicting protein-protein interactions (Park & Marcotte)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: distinguishes negative subsets for testing (must be unbiased so estimates generalize to population) from training subsets.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Supports recommending random (unbiased) negatives for evaluation.

papers.title: Current Time Series Anomaly Detection Benchmarks are Flawed and are Creating the Illusion of Progress (Wu & Keogh)
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: most exemplars of popular TSAD benchmarks have one of four flaws (triviality, unrealistic anomaly density, mislabeled ground truth, run-to-failure bias; flaw names quoted by CARE paper).
papers.overlap_with_claim: Benchmark-flaw genre; none of the four flaws is about how the negative/normal class is selected.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection: How to Artificially Increase Your F1-Score with a Biased Evaluation Protocol (Fourure et al.)
papers.what_it_shows: No abstract retrievable via OpenAlex/Crossref; title only. Known topic (not verified now): F1 depends on test-set contamination ratio.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Relates to the base-rate half of our argument, not negative selection. UNVERIFIED content.

papers.title: Reproducibility package for 'Detection without discrimination: a blinded, pre-registered test of pre-fault signals in public wind-turbine SCADA data' (Song)
papers.what_it_shows: Package downloaded; manuscript text grepped. Uses CARE normal events (farms B,C) and control windows (Kelmarsh/Penmanshiel) with 1000 random half-splits for an alarm-budget threshold.
papers.overlap_with_claim: No comparison of curated CARE normal events against random ordinary-operation windows from the same assets.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Residual Conformal Monitoring of Wind Turbine SCADA Data for Cross-Asset Anomaly Detection Under Distribution Shift
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: CARE v6 (45 anomalous/50 normal); alarms in 18 of 50 normal cases; argues same-asset calibration gives optimistic thresholds.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Uses curated normal cases as the false-alarm denominator; no random-window comparison.

papers.title: Chronologically calibrated PCA for wind-turbine SCADA health monitoring: a leakage-controlled CARE v6 benchmark
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: leakage-controlled CARE evaluation, normal-case accuracy and false-positive events on locked test turbines.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Leakage, not negative selection; no random-window comparison.

papers.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: deployment-style PHM benchmark; published accuracies rest on papers' own conventions (e.g., RUL capping can halve error).
papers.overlap_with_claim: Evaluation-convention optimism in PHM generally; not negative selection.

papers.title: Benchmarking Time-Series Anomaly Detection Algorithms for Photovoltaic Plants
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract: TimeEval benchmark on PV datasets with injected/controlled faults and fault-free days.
papers.overlap_with_claim: No curated-vs-random normal comparison.

papers.title: Challenges in detection of heating curve misconfiguration: An empirical study
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract (cites PreDist): CAE normal-behaviour model fails on gradual heating-curve drifts within normal ranges.
papers.overlap_with_claim: Not about negative selection.
